title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 23–25): Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'tame' combinatorics on a totally ordered set I. M = M(I) is a set of 'structures': points {a}, intervals I_{<a}, I_{a,b}, and so on. M carries order-type relations (⊴, ≪, |0|). On top of this he defines regions, polygons, constructible parts and 'ateliers', the structures to which constructible subsets are attached. The theorem being proved, started on p.23, is the following.
(a) For a constructible polygon 𝔓, the induced structure M(𝔓) is the direct sum of the M(𝔓_i) over the connected components 𝔓_i. This direct sum of 'magiciens'/ateliers is defined on p.25 as a disjoint union with sum orders.
(b) For connected 𝔓, M(𝔓) ≅ M(I', Ω0, Ω1). Here I' is a totally ordered set and Ω0, Ω1 are boundary data, each either empty or a single endpoint.

This page completes the description of (I', Ω0, Ω1) for a connected 𝔓, which is a chain 𝔏 of structures:
- Attach to each structure X its ordered support |X|° ⊂ I with the induced order. This support may be empty.
- I' is the lexicographic ordinal sum of the |X|°, X ∈ 𝔏, taken in the order ≤ of M.
- Ω0 = ∅ if the first structure of 𝔏 has no origin (it is an I_{<a}), or if its origin a is not in 𝔏. Otherwise Ω0 = {a = or(𝔏)}.
- Ω1 is defined dually, via the extremity.
- An NB says the origin (resp. extremity) of such a chain must still be defined formally.

Second part: definition of 'M divisible', i.e. a density condition, according to the boundary type.
- Case (I, ω0, ω1): for a<b in I there is c with a<c<b.
- Cases (I, ω0), resp. (I, ω1): add that every a has some b<a, resp. b>a. This is a 'no minimum / no maximum' condition on the open side.
- 'Biconvex'/open case: add I ≠ ∅. So the empty ordered set is declared not divisible, even though M(∅) = {∅}. This is a convention comparable to declaring the empty space not connected.
- In the full open case, divisibility of I therefore amounts to I being a dense linear order without endpoints, i.e. a model of DLO.
- Claim: if I is divisible, the subset M_c ⊂ M of 'compact' structures (points {a} and closed intervals I_{a,b}) is 'very dense' in M.

Purpose: a normal form for the induced tame structure on connected 1-dimensional constructible pieces, as a step toward a 1-dimensional 'topologie modérée' over an arbitrary ordered set.
errors: The boundary conventions are ambiguous. If ω0, ω1 denote adjoined endpoints outside I, then density in the case (I, ω0, ω1) should also require I ≠ ∅, no minimum and no maximum, not merely density between points of I. If instead ω0, ω1 are endpoints belonging to I, then the side conditions for (I, ω0) and (I, ω1) look swapped. Either way the case list on the page is not fully consistent as written.
The definition of Ω0 is incomplete. The clause 'origin a ∉ ... 𝔏' is partly illegible, and the notion of the origin of the chain is explicitly left undefined in the NB.
'Très dense' for M_c is asserted without proof and without specifying which relation (⊴ or ≪) the density refers to.

ideas.what: Induced structure on a connected constructible 1-dim polygon is the lexicographic (ordinal) sum of the supports of the structures in the chain, with boundary data Ω0, Ω1 given by origin and extremity
ideas.modern_name: Ordinal sum of linear orders; cell decomposition / normal form of definable sets in 1-dim o-minimal structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ordinal sums: Cantor/Hausdorff. Normal form of definable subsets in dimension 1: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorst (1984–86)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; this formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: Divisibility of an ordered set relative to endpoint type, with the empty ordered set excluded
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cantor (characterisation of Q); model theory of DLO

ideas.what: When I is dense, the 'compact' structures (points and closed intervals) are very dense in M
ideas.modern_name: Density of closed bounded cells among definable cells

missed.claim: These pages develop an axiomatic 1-dimensional tame-topology formalism ('ateliers', 'magiciens', polygons, constructible parts) over an arbitrary totally ordered set, in the same year as Pillay–Steinhorst / Knight–Pillay–Steinhorst on o-minimality. This page's normal form (connected pieces as ordinal sums plus endpoint data, with divisibility playing the role of DLO) parallels the o-minimal cell description in dimension 1. The atelier formalism itself is undocumented in the literature. This particular page, however, is routine.
missed.quote: I est la somme (lexicographique) des |X|° (X ∈ 𝔏), se suivant dans l'ordre ≤ de M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents how Grothendieck concretely tried to realise the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse combinatorially, independently of model theory. Historians comparing his programme with o-minimality would find a concrete point of contact here.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary order theory: ordinal sums and density conditions. Its interest lies only in being part of the unpublished 'ateliers' attempt at tame topology, which parallels o-minimality.
transcription_corrections: 'que la relation d'ordre induite' is likely 'avec la relation d'ordre induite'.
The left margin note reads roughly 'cette description [...] lexicographique', tied to the inserted '(lexicographique)'.
'l'origine d'une projection' may read 'l'origine d'une progression' (i.e. the chain 𝔏); uncertain.
The final parenthesis likely reads '... on y fera attention pendant la suite!' or similar; uncertain.
